data.title: AI Hallucination
data.tagline: An AI hallucination is information a model generates that looks credible but is inaccurate, unsupported, or invented.
data.learningOutcome: You can decide when online research is needed and find verifiable primary sources for facts that affect a real plan.
data.description: An AI can invent venue hours, a nonexistent link, an outdated rule, or a function that is not in a project. Fluent wording is not evidence. An Agent can research changing external facts online, but conclusions still need official or original sources, tool results, tests, and human judgment.

learning.assumes: You have seen AI provide a complete guide, explanation, or answer with no source.
learning.outcome: You can decide when online research is needed and find verifiable primary sources for facts that affect a real plan.

explanation.title: A model generates; it does not inherently collect evidence
explanation.text: A model is good at organizing language from patterns, but can fill gaps with plausible details when context is missing, material is outdated, or no single answer exists.

explanation.title: Online research must lead to primary sources
explanation.text: For changing external facts such as opening hours, policies, or prices, an Agent can research online. Open the official site, announcement, or original file, then check publication date, applicability, and whether independent sources agree. A search summary or secondary repost alone leaves the claim uncertain.

data.boundary: An AI hallucination is not the source of every mistake, and connecting to the web does not guarantee correctness. Tool and search results can still be outdated, irrelevant, or misread; high-stakes decisions require original sources and applicability checks.

lessonPractice.title: AI says the city museum is open until 10 PM on Monday and puts it in the evening itinerary. What is the best action?

options.label: Research the museum's official website, official reservation page, and daily sessions online, then check the date before keeping it in the itinerary
options.feedback: Correct. Dated primary sources can verify opening hours directly; a search summary or detailed AI wording cannot replace official information.

options.label: Follow the guide because it includes a specific time
options.feedback: A precise time makes the claim sound real but does not prove accuracy. Arriving to find it closed would disrupt the trip.

options.label: Keep asking the same AI if it is sure without checking another source
options.feedback: Repeated confirmation from the same model is not independent evidence. Return to the official site, official reservation page, or venue notice.

data.agentPrompt: My family will use this AI-generated travel guide. Research every venue's opening hours and reservation rules online, prioritizing official websites, announcements, or reservation pages. Include the source link and publication or update date. Mark claims supported only by search summaries, secondary reposts, or no original source as uncertain, and do not invent links. Remove closed or unavailable visits after checking.
